newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on foreign capital inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on foreign capital inflow.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed stronger on Friday for the second day in a row on an inflow of foreign capital into Mexico following an early fall in U.S. long bond rates, traders said.
"U.S. employment and unemployment data brought long bond yields down and thus triggered an inflow of foreign capital," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.55 and 0.8 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8050/7.8080 and 7.8020/7.8050 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso closed 1.3 centavos firmer on the week.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 2.55 centavos firmer at 7.7890/7.7920 per dollar.
Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury fell to 6.68 percent in early trade, from 6.76 percent on Thursday, but increased to 6.72 percent when the foreign exchange trading closed in Mexico.

Dealers noted 48-hour contracts failed to break the 7.80 per dollar barrier, but said they could do so next week if January inflation figures, due out after the close of trade on Friday, were within market expectations.
A Reuters survey MXAAP of nine financial houses in Mexico City showed an average forecast rise of 2.4 percent for consumer prices in January.
